figures.caption: Figure 1: Architecture of our proposed HRF-Res. The external input ut is projected into a LIF encoder population (left, pink) via the fixed matrix U. LIF spikes sLIF t are passed to the HRF oscillatory reservoir (right, blue) via V; each HRF neuron oscillates at its own resonance frequency and feeds spikes sHRF t back to the LIF layer via W. All weights are fixed; only the linear readout r = WoyT + bo is trained.

Figure 2: Band-pass properties of HRF-Res vs. LIF-Res. (A) Fraction of resonant neurons (Q > 0) per dataset. HRF-Res has 4–20× more resonant neurons than LIF-Res, confirming that band-pass dynamics survive in a full spiking reservoir setting. (B) Mean Q-factor among resonant neurons. HRF neurons form sharper band-pass filters on all datasets, with the largest gaps on FordA (4.6 vs. 2.0), DVS Gesture (3.4 vs. 1.4) and SHD (2.5 vs. 0.6). Bars show mean ± std over three seeds.

Figure 3: HRF-Res produces more class-discriminative representations. (A) CKA between temporal mean reservoir states and category labels (mean ± std over three seeds). HRF-Res achieves higher CKA than LIF-Res on all four datasets. (B) Distribution of per-neuron preferred frequencies (log scale). HRF neurons show distributed tuning across a range of frequencies, consistent with a heterogeneous bank of band-pass filters; LIF neurons collapse to the lowest sweep frequency, consistent with pure integration.

Table 1: HRF-Res vs. LIF-Res. Both architectures are otherwise identical; hyperparameters for LIF-Res are independently re-tuned per dataset. Results are mean ± std over 5 seeds with final reservoir state readout. HRF-Res outperforms or matches LIF-Res on all four datasets, with accuracy gains up to +26.6% and lower energy consumption on most datasets. See Appendix A.5 for LIFRes architecture details and Appendix A.4 for the evaluation protocol.

Table 3: Comparison with spiking reservoir baselines. Neurons: number of reservoir units. HRFRes results: mean ± std over 5 seeds. HRF-Res achieves competitive or state-of-the-art accuracy across all modalities, in most cases with fewer neurons than prior methods.
